target: tr_M(D, q_0)  [canonical Wenzl-bridge, post-PR #612]  [CONVENTION-C, CODATA-2018 MUON PIN — scoped 2026-08-30, qou-rm57]
description:
Step-by-step derivation of D's Schur-Weyl trace τ_SW(D, q_0) ≈ 0.17743692421543206. CORRECTION (2026-04-28): the value computed here is τ_SW = Σ_λ [s_λ(q,q⁻¹)/H_q(λ)] χ_λ — the Schur-Weyl / Reshetikhin-Turaev-at-SU(2) functional, NOT the canonical Jones-Markov trace τ_M. The two differ: τ_SW(σ_i) ≈ 0.883 at q_0 vs τ_M(σ_i) = z ≈ 0.499 (Markov axiom). The previous label 'tr_M' (suggesting Jones-Markov) was structurally wrong — see prop:markov-trace-frobenius-selection. Use the parallel derivation chain `D-tau-M-q0.derivation.json` for the canonical Jones-Markov trace τ_M(D) ≈ 0.336821.

CONVENTION AND PIN SCOPING (2026-08-30, bean `qou-rm57`). This document is
DOUBLY off canon, and neither departure was declared:

  1. CONVENTION C. Its numbers use the Markov parameter z = sqrt(q)/(q+1).
     The owner ruling of 2026-08-15 makes convention D (z = q^3/(q^2+1))
     canonical. Live D value for this atom, at the canonical proton pin:
         tr_M(D) = 0.575172243917771870826535343986180889152494352892855072730158
     (source: computations/atomic-tr-m-mpfr-50dps-proton.witness.json, and
     derivation_chain.py::TR_M_AT_Q0, which therefore DISAGREES with the
     target_value above.)

  2. THE MUON PIN USED IS NEITHER LIVE ANCHOR. Step 7 evaluates at
     q_0 = 1.1099785955541805 — the CODATA-2018 lepton-tower derivation, not
     the frozen canonical muon pin (1.1099785955573347...) and not the proton
     pin the 2026-08-15 ruling makes default for compute.

     Established rather than assumed: the target differs from the exact
     convention-C proton trace at the FROZEN muon pin by rel 1.9504e-11,
     while dq/q between the two muon pins is 2.8417e-12 — an elasticity of
     6.86, which is exactly the scale a Laurent polynomial spanning q^-6..q^6
     gives (the proton braid word has 6 crossings; chi^(3) = q^6,
     chi^(111) = q^-6). Float64 truncation is REFUTED as the explanation: it
     would agree to ~1e-16, not diverge at the 11th digit.

The DERIVATION is not in question — the Hecke presentation, Wedderburn
decomposition, Schur-Weyl weights and Frobenius pairing are all
convention-independent. Only the evaluation carries the frame.

Kept as recorded, not corrected: the values are right for their own frame and
pin, and re-deriving under D at the proton pin is a compute, not an edit.

CROSS-FAMILY DISAGREEMENT (same pass). The corpus carries TWO derivation
chains for this quantity — `D-tr-M-q0.derivation.json` and `markov-trace-assembly-deuteron.derivation.json` —
and their target_values differ by rel 1.223e-7 while BOTH declare
target_tolerance 1e-09. That is 122x the tolerance they each assert.

The proton pair agrees exactly (rel 0.0), so this is not a systematic offset
between the two methods; it is specific to this atom. Which of the two is
right is NOT established here. Tracked in `qou-rm57`.

steps.name: Hecke algebra H_6(q) presentation
steps.operation: Define H_6(q) := ⟨σ_1..σ_5 | braid relations, Hecke relation (σ_i - q)(σ_i + q^{-1}) = 0⟩.
steps.notes: Hecke energy axiom: each σ_i carries σ_i^2 = (q-q^{-1})σ_i + 1; the (q-q^{-1}) factor is the per-crossing energy (AGENTS.md §7a).

steps.name: Wedderburn decomposition of H_6(q)
steps.operation: H_6(q) ≅ ⊕_{λ ⊢ 6} M_{f_λ}(K(q)) (semisimple at generic q, including q_0).
steps.notes: Partitions of 6 index the simple factors; Hoefsmit frame dimensions f_λ from `schur_weyl_symbolic.partitions_of`.  Mathlib backs the abstract direct-sum statement via `Algebra.Algebraic.Module.WedderburnArtin`.

steps.name: Schur–Weyl weights w_λ(q)
steps.operation: For each λ, compute w_λ(q) per Schur–Weyl duality U_q(sl_2) ↺ V^{⊗3A}; Hoefsmit normalisation (Kassel §III.4).
steps.notes: script: computations/schur_weyl_symbolic.py function `schur_weyl_weight(lam, q)`.  SCRIPT_CITED pending its own derivation chain.

steps.name: Categorical action B_6 → ⊕_λ M_{f_λ}
steps.operation: Categorical action of B_6 on V^{⊗3A} via the R-matrix; project to each λ-block to get ρ^λ : H → M_{f_λ}(K(q)).
steps.output_value: ρ^λ for each λ — see hecke_character_symbolic.py
steps.notes: script: computations/hecke/hecke_character_symbolic.py Hoefsmit-matrix evaluation of σ_i.  SCRIPT_CITED.

steps.name: Atomic D braid word T_w(Z=1, N=1)
steps.operation: Atomic braid recipe: Z=1 up-strands, N=1 down-strands, include_inter=True; produces a word with 12 crossings on 6 strands.
steps.notes: script: computations/hecke/hecke_character_symbolic.py function `atomic_braid_to_crossings`.  SCRIPT_CITED — the atomic-braid recipe itself awaits formalisation.

steps.name: Frobenius pairing — characters χ^λ_q(T_w)
steps.operation: For each λ, compute χ^λ_q(T_w) := tr(ρ^λ(T_w)) (Frobenius pairing identifies traces with characters of the regular rep).
steps.output_value: χ^λ_q(T_w) Laurent polynomial in q for each λ ⊢ 6

steps.name: Markov trace via finite-Jones formula
steps.operation: tr_M(T_w, q) := Σ_{λ ⊢ 6} w_λ(q) · χ^λ_q(T_w); uniqueness from the Markov property + finite-Jones.
steps.output_value: symbolic Laurent polynomial in q (Markov trace)
steps.notes: Derivation chain: markov-trace-assembly-deuteron.derivation.json.  Combines schur-weyl-weight-{6, 51, 42, 411, 33, 321, 3111, 222, 2211, 21111, 111111} (all 11 partitions of n=3·A=6) + chi-deuteron-h6.witness.json (per-irrep characters χ^λ_q(β_D) via hecke_character_symbolic.q_character_on_braid_word, cached); the σ-word β_D for the deuteron is derived via `atomic-braid-recipe-d.derivation.json` (chain reference).  Step trust upgrades from SCRIPT_CITED to DERIVED via the assembly chain reference.
